filedLate: This CP1 records the design as executed. It was written after the first build pass rather than before it, which is a process miss and is stated rather than backdated.

planForTheTitle.criterion: 2.4.2 Page Titled (WCAG 2.0 A / Rev508). Also answers 2.4.6 Headings and Labels indirectly by naming the surface.
planForTheTitle.whyAxeCannotSeeIt: axe scans one page at a time and a title is present on every page. Nav items and tabs are real <a href> full navigations, so each is a distinct page, and the criterion fails only under a comparison ACROSS surfaces.
planForTheTitle.shape: <surface> [ · <parent surface> ] · <city> · SmartCity Dashboards. Most specific first, because a screen reader announces the title on arrival and reads left to right.
whereItIsResolved: src/staff-review.mjs surfaceTitle() is the ONE resolver. The three label maps moved there out of web/app.js rather than being copied.
The EXISTING G-89 inline head script in web/index.html carries the forced second copy and stamps document.title before the parser reaches the body. No second script is added.

web/app.js appends the pack name once GET /api/city-identity resolves, passing identity.documentTitle as the tail. The surface part is never late; only the city, which this product does not assert unread.
planForTheTitle.howTheSecondCopyIsHeld: src/first-paint.test.mjs whitelistDivergences() extended to compare PRODUCT_TITLE, TITLE_SEP and all four label maps textually AND to compare the resolved title behaviourally for every query probe. Maps are compared by value, not by key set, because a RENAMED label puts a word in the title that appears nowhere on the screen while every id still resolves.
planForTheTitle.watchedFailing: A late-title build is constructed inside the test by deleting the document.title line from the head script; the same acceptance predicate is asserted to throw with actual 'SmartCity Dashboards' and expected 'Overview · SmartCity Dashboards'. The whole test file was additionally run against a mutated web/index.html and its raw failure recorded.
planForTheTitle.staticTitleKept: web/index.html keeps <title>SmartCity Dashboards</title>. With scripting off nothing stamps data-surface, every URL paints Overview, and the document really is one page - so one product-level title is the honest answer there, not a fallback claiming a surface the browser is not showing.

planForTheGate.ci: .github/workflows/ci.yml gains a second REQUIRED job `a11y` running npm ci, npx playwright-core install --with-deps chromium, npm run test:a11y
planForTheGate.whyASeparateJob: npm test is `node --test src/*.test.mjs` on a bare Node image, and src/hidden-rule.test.mjs and src/first-paint.test.mjs both already rule that a check which quietly skips when Chrome is absent is a control that never fires. The browser check therefore does not join that suite pretending to be optional.
planForTheGate.noSkipPath: A missing or unlaunchable browser exits 2 with the install command in the message. There is no branch in the file that can exit 0 without having scanned.
survivesAFreshClone: axe comes from the axe-core devDependency, not from P:/tmp/VPAT/axe.min.js on one machine

the browser comes from playwright-core plus an explicit install step; playwright-core is chosen over playwright precisely because it downloads no browser on npm install, so the ordinary test job stays cheap
the server under test is this repo's own src/server.mjs started in-process on an ephemeral port; nothing deployed, no port hardcoded, process exits
planForTheGate.derivedNotHardcoded: Targets are built in src/a11y-surfaces.mjs from ALL_LENS_IDS, DS_TABS, WORK_IDS, ASSET_TABS (src/staff-review.mjs) and the packs in src/city-pack.mjs; themes from THEMES in src/theme.mjs. A lens or a theme added later is scanned with no edit here.
planForTheGate.surfaceDenominator: 23 surfaces, not the 16 the baseline used. Every tab is a real href, so a tab is a surface exactly as a lens is. BASELINE_SURFACES names the 16-surface subset so the before/after figures stay comparable against the recorded baseline.
planForTheGate.exitBounded: fixed target list, browser closed in a finally, server closed in a finally, process exits with a code.

adversarialReview.risk: The gate can never be green, because color-contrast is a sibling lane's fix.
adversarialReview.ruling: DEV_PROCESS 2.0: a permanently-red gate is a dead gate. The contract is SPLIT - zero tolerance everywhere, one named waiver with its owner, its basis and its removal condition. The waiver is a RATCHET: above the pin fails, below the pin prints a loud STALE line, zero on every theme FAILS with an instruction to delete the entry. An exception that can only ever be satisfied is the control that never fires.

adversarialReview.risk: A waiver stated as one total lets a dark regression hide behind a light improvement.
adversarialReview.ruling: Pinned PER THEME. Two pins cannot be compensated against each other.

adversarialReview.risk: A green gate that never actually ran the palette it claims to have scanned.
adversarialReview.ruling: Two guards. Every scan asserts document.documentElement's data-theme is the one it asked for. The run asserts the two themes PAINT differently, and fails if every surface renders both identically - the divergence test for the lever itself.

adversarialReview.risk: Class discipline. A markup fix that needs a new class triggers a kit re-vendor.
adversarialReview.ruling: Zero new classes. The defined vocabulary stays at 143 (src/shell-parity.test.mjs counting rule: served stylesheets, CRLF-normalized, comments stripped, every dot-identifier, deduplicated). The heading fix reuses .state h2, which web/shell.css already styled; the scrollable fix is a tabindex attribute; the status fix is an aria-live attribute.

adversarialReview.risk: web/sc-kit.css is the sibling lane's and a token edit forks the system.
adversarialReview.ruling: Not touched. Verified by git diff: the file is not in this branch's change set.

constraintsAccepted: no invented freshness; no last sync / last read / last updated added
no real city asserted as content
live Bastrop no-touch; G-52 not started; G-24 not filled; L26 untouched
openAtCp1: Whether the waiver pin survives G-94 merging first. If it does not, the pin is re-measured and re-pinned; that is the designed forcing function, not a defect.
